changes.place: L2 participle in the first parenthesis

The middle letter has a deep descending p stroke. Rencontrent has no such medial descender. The low preceding r/e/c/o/u sequence and following e/n/t strokes support recoupent.

changes.evidence: A long curved connector from the raised words lands just after the opening parenthesis and before the q of quadratiques. It does not attach after d’intersection. Each quotation mark is a pair of short vertical ticks, not a guillemet. The main-line i.e. remains before les pts singuliers. Abbreviation reading is logged separately.

The initial sign is a tall undotted stroke, favoring sc. over ie.; the following tiny connected loop does not securely distinguish c from e. Only the final stop is plain. Retain both readings, with sc. first, rather than resolve by meaning.
The c/o, low r/r/e and descending p are followed by the o/n/d sequence. After the tall d, a short e-like dash precedes the joined n/t ending; no rounded a is visible there.

changes.place: L10 adverb before aux pts doubles
changes.evidence: The initial b and dotted i are followed by low u/n/i/v/o strokes and a clear long q descender in the middle. The final u/e/m/e/n/t sequence follows. Bijectivement would not account for that medial q.

changes.place: L13 loop noun after n’a pas de
changes.evidence: The b/o/u/c/l sequence ends in one small final e-stroke with a trailing exit. No independent terminal s follows it. This is distinct from the earlier plural boucles on L9, which remains plural.
The tall f and low e/r/m strokes are followed by accented e and a separate final e. Blank paper intervenes before the comma; there is no added s. The earlier fermées on L9 remains plural.
Two upright t stems share a horizontal crossbar, with a short exit stroke after the second. There are no o/u letters between them. Preserve the abbreviation.
The low u/n sequence has an additional final low ending, comparable to the clear une before composante earlier on the page. Retain une before the hatted X rather than regularize its gender.

changes.place: L18 shorthand and following word, M0933
changes.evidence: The shorthand consists of two continuous horizontal strokes. The lower one is slightly wavy, but there are no separate m stems under a bar. The following word has a small reduced a, shallow v, low e and terminal c strokes, giving avec. This resolves the first C alternative without expanding the sign in the transcription.
A faint closed upper loop and long descending curved tail form 9 at the lower-left edge. It is separate from the dark top pagination 4. Its position does not establish that the same hand wrote it.

Two continuous horizontal strokes, the lower slightly wavy, with no separate m stems. It is the literal equals-shaped shorthand before the readable word avec.

doubts.reason: The initial undotted tall sign favors sc., but the compact connected second glyph does not decide c/e. The preferred first reading differs from C and is logged as a cropped change.

doubts.place: L17 first word of the cancellation
doubts.reason: The first à is almost absorbed by the horizontal strike. The l, apostrophe, a/i/d/e of l’aide remain readable. This new uncertainty keeps C’s primary letters unchanged, so it is recorded only as a doubt.
B09: two upright t stems share a crossbar. A separate low curved exit after the second can be the end flourish or a very reduced e. Keep tt preferred without forcing agreement with arc.
B10: after the p descender is a tiny round trace before the hyphen. It can be reduced o or an abbreviation point. Do not expand the fragment or decide it from the next, unsupplied page.

notes: The page explains the graph of a curve: irreducible components correspond to vertices, singular intersection points to edges, and loops at a vertex to double points of the corresponding component. It then states that smooth components correspond to a graph without a closed loop, expressed by distinct origin and endpoint for every arc. This is a transcription summary, not an independent verification of the statements.

The final paragraph says that any finite graph can be obtained, up to isomorphism, from a suitable hatted X; the page ends with compo-. The divided word is left exactly at the page boundary. The author replaced the phrase à l’aide by par une and inserted (à iso près) before the cancellation.

The source has figurés and une; these are retained without grammatical regularization. Recoupent is selected from the medial p descender. Biunivoquement is selected from its long medial q descender. The last occurrence is singular boucle fermée, while the earlier phrase boucles fermées en alpha remains plural.

The raised quotation belongs inside the parenthesis before quadratiques, not after d’intersection. Its quotation marks are paired ticks. M0932 remains sc.|ie.; M0933 is resolved to the two-stroke equals-shaped shorthand, used as a verbal shorthand; its proposed expansion is confined to the abbreviations list.

There are two visible pagination marks: dark 4 at the top and light 9 at the bottom left. The bottom mark is catalogued as unidentified hand (light pagination), not attributed to the author from its position alone. H’s editorial note about top page 4 is not transcribed as prose.

Line count 22 = 18 main text baselines, two raised insertion baselines, and the two pagination baselines. No independent diagram or displayed equation occurs on this sheet; the curved strokes are insertion connectors. Dashes rendered by different TeX or Unicode conventions in the witnesses are not treated as substantive differences.

Original and both native halves, followed by each of the ten saved crops, were inspected once. No OCR, web lookup, TeX compilation or independent mathematical check was used. No symbolic origin o or sigma occurs on this page; origine is written as a word. All C=H words and inline symbols were read against the ink.

Blind B06 spans the complete two-baseline passage around biunivoquement, leaving room for its long q descender; it does not cut that word at a tight line boundary. The only written numerals on this sheet, top 4 and light bottom 9, have B01 and B11 respectively.

Independent audit: the top numeral is an angular open 4. The final curve after tt and the tiny trace before the hyphen in compo- are now explicitly doubtful (tt/tte; compo-/comp.-). Their preferred primary readings are unchanged. The singular boucle and fermée have no independently visible extra s. The raised sc./ie. abbreviation and the canceled initial à remain uncertain. The verbal shorthand keeps two near-parallel strokes without a separate m body. No independent mathematical check was performed.
